name: Simon I of Alexandria
knownFor: Coptic patriarch of Alexandria, a Syrian chosen over his own teacher. The History tells how he survived poison, and would not ordain a bishop for India without the governor's leave.
dates: B. Evetts heads his life 689 to 701, and René Basset's French of the Arabic Synaxarium brackets 689 to 702. The History says he died on the 24th of the Coptic month Abib, in the year 416 of Diocletian, after nine and a half years. Eusèbe Renaudot gives seven years and six months, and reads the year as 415
place: Born in the East, the History says. Brought up at the monastery of Az-Zajaj, and buried there. The History says the body of Saint Severus lies in a shrine there. Budge's Ethiopic names him Severus of Antioch, and the synaxaria place the monastery west of Alexandria
role: Patriarch of Alexandria, the forty-second in the History's count

traces: He wrote a synodical letter to Julian, patriarch of Antioch, on the unity of their two sees. Julian answered and sent back rich gifts, the History says.
He ordained Zacharias bishop of Sakha and Ptolemy bishop of Upper Manuf, among many others, the History says.
John the deacon, who wrote the History's life of Michael I, says Simon's archdeacon George wrote its account from Cyril of Alexandria to Alexander II.
remembered: The Arabic Synaxarium, the Coptic church's book of saints' days, keeps him on the 24th of Abib in René Basset's French. Like the History, it has the priests freed and the magicians burned.
The Ethiopic Synaxarium, in E. A. Wallis Budge's English, keeps him on the 24th of Hamle. It has him sick for four days, and the priests sent into exile.
Eusèbe Renaudot, a Catholic scholar writing in Latin in 1713, says the Copts keep his memory on the 24th of Abib.
A book on the churches of Egypt, under the name of Abu Salih, calls him Simon the Syrian. It dates a monastery at Hulwan to his time and Isaac's.

uncertain: His life rests on the History of the Patriarchs, a later Arabic history of the Coptic church. Its life of Simon names no writer.

Who wrote these years. John the deacon says George's history ran from Cyril to the days of Alexander II, down to the time of the caliph Sulaiman. Renaudot gives George the same end point. He says many wrote the lives from Cyril to Simon, George above all.
The poisoning. The History says he lay forty days and recovered. Budge's Ethiopic says four days. Renaudot reports the historian Elmacinus, who says a fourth dose killed him.
The poisoners. The History and Basset's synaxarium say the priests were freed at his plea. Budge's Ethiopic and Renaudot say they were exiled.
The cups. B. Evetts's English of the History has his cup poisoned twice before the figs. Renaudot's reading of the History, Basset's synaxarium and Budge's Ethiopic have three times.
His years. The History gives nine and a half, Renaudot seven years and six months.
The order of patriarchs. Michael the Syrian, a twelfth-century patriarch of the Syriac Orthodox church, puts Simon before Isaac. The History puts him after.
